revision.summary: Weather describes atmospheric conditions at a particular time; climate is the long-term average pattern. Elements include temperature, pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation. Climate controls include latitude, altitude, pressure and winds, distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief. India’s climate is strongly influenced by the monsoon, a seasonal reversal of wind direction. Differential heating, the seasonal shift of the ITCZ and upper-air circulation help shape it. The Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches bring rainfall to different regions. The Himalayas influence the movement of monsoon winds. The cold weather season broadly occurs from December to February; the hot weather season from March to May. The advancing southwest monsoon generally brings rain from June to September. During retreating monsoon, October–November, the Tamil Nadu coast receives important rainfall. Rainfall is high on windward slopes of the Western Ghats and in parts of northeast India; western Rajasthan and Ladakh are comparatively dry. Uneven monsoon rainfall can cause floods, droughts and crop losses. Rainwater harvesting and watershed management improve resilience.
